questions.questionText: What is the LCM of 15, 25 and 48?
questions.explanation: Prime factorisations: 15 = 3 x 5; 25 = 5^2; 48 = 2^4 x 3. LCM = product of the highest powers of each prime = 1200.
questions.shortcut: Take every prime at its highest power across the numbers.

questions.questionText: What is the LCM of 15, 40 and 48?
questions.explanation: Prime factorisations: 15 = 3 x 5; 40 = 2^3 x 5; 48 = 2^4 x 3. LCM = product of the highest powers of each prime = 240.
questions.shortcut: Take every prime at its highest power across the numbers.

questions.questionText: What is the LCM of 15, 16 and 25?
questions.explanation: Prime factorisations: 15 = 3 x 5; 16 = 2^4; 25 = 5^2. LCM = product of the highest powers of each prime = 1200.
questions.shortcut: Take every prime at its highest power across the numbers.

questions.questionText: What is the LCM of 12, 15 and 42?
questions.explanation: Prime factorisations: 12 = 2^2 x 3; 15 = 3 x 5; 42 = 2 x 3 x 7. LCM = product of the highest powers of each prime = 420.
questions.shortcut: Take every prime at its highest power across the numbers.

questions.questionText: What is the LCM of 16, 45 and 54?
questions.explanation: Prime factorisations: 16 = 2^4; 45 = 3^2 x 5; 54 = 2 x 3^3. LCM = product of the highest powers of each prime = 2160.
questions.shortcut: Take every prime at its highest power across the numbers.

questions.questionText: What is the LCM of 15, 16 and 24?
questions.explanation: Prime factorisations: 15 = 3 x 5; 16 = 2^4; 24 = 2^3 x 3. LCM = product of the highest powers of each prime = 240.
questions.shortcut: Take every prime at its highest power across the numbers.

questions.questionText: Find the LCM of 12, 15, 30 and 35.
questions.explanation: Prime factorisations: 12 = 2^2 x 3; 15 = 3 x 5; 30 = 2 x 3 x 5; 35 = 5 x 7. LCM = 420.
questions.shortcut: Highest power of each prime appearing in any number.

questions.questionText: Find the LCM of 9, 21, 30 and 35.
questions.explanation: Prime factorisations: 9 = 3^2; 21 = 3 x 7; 30 = 2 x 3 x 5; 35 = 5 x 7. LCM = 630.
questions.shortcut: Highest power of each prime appearing in any number.

questions.questionText: Find the HCF of 7/5, 6/7, 10/9.
questions.explanation: HCF of fractions = HCF of numerators / LCM of denominators = HCF(7, 6, 10) / LCM(5, 7, 9) = 1/315 = 1/315.
questions.shortcut: HCF(fractions) = HCF(numerators) / LCM(denominators).

questions.explanation: Product of two numbers = HCF x LCM. Other number = (7 x 294)/98 = 21.

questions.questionText: What is the greatest number that divides 451 and 204 leaving a remainder of 14 in each case?
questions.explanation: Required number = HCF(451 - 14, 204 - 14) = HCF(437, 190) = 19.

questions.questionText: What is the greatest number that divides 235 leaving remainder 1 and divides 382 leaving remainder 5?
questions.explanation: The number divides 235 - 1 = 234 and 382 - 5 = 377 exactly. HCF(234, 377) = 13.
questions.shortcut: Subtract each number's own remainder, then take the HCF of the results.

questions.questionText: What is the greatest number that divides 237 leaving remainder 13 and divides 592 leaving remainder 4?
questions.explanation: The number divides 237 - 13 = 224 and 592 - 4 = 588 exactly. HCF(224, 588) = 28.

questions.shortcut: Subtract each number's own remainder, then take the HCF of the results.

questions.questionText: What is the smallest number which, when divided by 4, 5 and 30, leaves a remainder of 3 in each case?
questions.explanation: LCM(4, 5, 30) = 60. Required number = 60 + 3 = 63.
questions.shortcut: LCM + common remainder.

questions.questionText: What is the smallest number which, when divided by 18, 20 and 30, leaves a remainder of 4 in each case?
questions.shortcut: LCM + common remainder.

questions.questionText: What is the smallest number which, when divided by 5, 6 and 8, leaves a remainder of 4 in each case?

questions.questionText: What is the smallest number which, when increased by 3, becomes exactly divisible by 6, 8 and 25?
questions.explanation: The number + 3 must be a multiple of LCM(6, 8, 25) = 600. Smallest number = 600 - 3 = 597.
questions.shortcut: LCM - the amount needed to reach a multiple.

questions.questionText: What is the smallest number which, when increased by 2, becomes exactly divisible by 8, 20 and 24?
questions.explanation: The number + 2 must be a multiple of LCM(8, 20, 24) = 120. Smallest number = 120 - 2 = 118.
questions.shortcut: LCM - the amount needed to reach a multiple.

questions.questionText: What is the smallest number which, when increased by 4, becomes exactly divisible by 8, 9 and 12?

questions.questionText: What is the smallest number which, when increased by 2, becomes exactly divisible by 6, 12 and 20?

questions.questionText: What is the smallest number which, when increased by 8, becomes exactly divisible by 15, 18 and 20?

questions.questionText: What is the smallest number which, when increased by 6, becomes exactly divisible by 15, 20 and 30?

questions.questionText: What is the smallest number which leaves remainder 4 when divided by 8, 15 or 16, and is exactly divisible by 11?
questions.explanation: Numbers of the form 240k + 4 (LCM = 240). Testing k = 1, 2, 3 and so on, the first one divisible by 11 is k = 2, giving 484.
questions.shortcut: Form LCM x k + remainder and test k until the extra condition holds.

questions.questionText: What is the smallest number which leaves remainder 3 when divided by 9, 18 or 20, and is exactly divisible by 7?
questions.explanation: Numbers of the form 180k + 3 (LCM = 180). Testing k = 1, 2, 3 and so on, the first one divisible by 7 is k = 5, giving 903.
questions.shortcut: Form LCM x k + remainder and test k until the extra condition holds.

questions.questionText: Three bells ring at intervals of 15, 36 and 40 seconds. If they ring together now, after how many seconds will they next ring together?
questions.explanation: They ring together again after LCM(15, 36, 40) = 360 seconds.
questions.shortcut: Time to coincide = LCM of the intervals.

questions.questionText: Three bells ring at intervals of 8, 40 and 60 seconds. If they ring together now, after how many seconds will they next ring together?
questions.explanation: They ring together again after LCM(8, 40, 60) = 120 seconds.
questions.shortcut: Time to coincide = LCM of the intervals.

questions.questionText: Three bells ring at intervals of 8, 10 and 15 seconds. If they ring together now, after how many seconds will they next ring together?

questions.shortcut: Time to coincide = LCM of the intervals.

questions.questionText: Three bells ring at intervals of 20, 36 and 45 seconds. If they ring together now, after how many seconds will they next ring together?
questions.explanation: They ring together again after LCM(20, 36, 45) = 180 seconds.
questions.shortcut: Time to coincide = LCM of the intervals.

questions.questionText: Three bells toll at intervals of 8, 24 and 30 seconds and all toll together at the start. How many times will they toll together in 60 minutes, including the one at the start?
questions.explanation: LCM = 120 s. In 60 minutes = 3600 s they toll together 3600//120 = 30 more times, plus the start: 31.
questions.shortcut: Count = (total time / LCM) + 1 including the start.

questions.questionText: A hall 185 m long and 444 m wide is to be paved with square stones of the same size. What is the least number of stones required?
questions.explanation: Side of largest stone = HCF(185, 444) = 37 m. Number = (185/37) x (444/37) = 5 x 12 = 60.
questions.shortcut: Least stones = (l x b) / (HCF)^2.

questions.questionText: Two numbers are in the ratio 4:9 and their HCF is 14. What is their LCM?
questions.explanation: The numbers are 4 x 14 = 56 and 9 x 14 = 126. LCM = 14 x 4 x 9 = 504.
questions.shortcut: For co-prime ratio p:q and HCF h, LCM = h x p x q.

questions.questionText: The sum of two numbers is 180, their HCF is 10 and their LCM is 770. What is the larger number?

questions.shortcut: Divide sum and LCM by the HCF to get m + n and mn.
